c0-frame.title: Frame cycle 1
c0-frame.imperative: Human picks flavor (recommending shotgun: diverge on HOW to keep user+agents on the same level before committing to the concepts-book/tutor shape). First cycle seeds from starting questions; several are pre-answered by the raw idea, so ask only the genuinely-open ones: kill condition, and what 'understanding' concretely means to the user.
c0-frame.finding: Flavor = shotgun (human accepted; ideas were partly human-sourced, so shotgun opened the space rather than steering).

q1-kill.title: Kill condition: what would make this pointless to build?
q1-kill.imperative: Starting-question 5. Genuinely unnamed. Candidate: 'this is a discipline problem (agents just need to follow the existing plain-language mandate), not a machinery problem — so building a concepts book + tutor is over-building.' Name it now, test it early.
q1-kill.finding: NO hard kill condition (human). Not a jargon-ban: user is expert enough to want precise jargon and refuses to be talked down to. Agents DO fail to follow plain talk -> need better-than-honor-system mechanism. Soft anti-goals instead: pointless/wrong if it (i) becomes heavy machinery for its own sake, (ii) bans precise jargon, or (iii) condescends.

q2-understanding.title: What does 'coming along for the ride' concretely mean?
q2-understanding.imperative: Sharpen 'done feels like'. Three grades of understanding: (a) not-surprised — the user recognizes terms and isn't blindsided; (b) can-decide — the user grasps a concept well enough to make the call that depends on it; (c) can-reconstruct — the user could explain/rebuild it themselves. Which grade is the target? This sets how hard teaching has to work.
q2-understanding.finding: Target = B (can-decide), reaching for C (can-reconstruct) where it matters. Context: expert in the domain but no formal stats / engineering-analysis training; learns by doing, not classes; wants peer register.

q3-shotgun.title: Diverge: ways to keep user and agents on the same level
q3-shotgun.imperative: If shotgun: generate ~15-20 cheap one-liners spanning the mechanism space (behavioral mandates, tracked artifacts, gates/lints, interactive teaching, register controls), wild entries welcome, so the user sees the space rather than only the concepts-book+tutor shape they arrived with.
q3-shotgun.finding: 20 ideas in 5 families. A=register/talk mandates: (1) plain-talk-default w/ teeth, (2) no-unagreed-shorthand until term 'unlocked', (3) first-use gloss required, (4) user-set register dial new<->peer, (5) jargon budget per message. B=tracked artifacts: (6) concepts book [user C2], (7) familiarity as USER-set dial 🟢🟡🔴, (8) extend GLOSSARY w/ provenance+familiarity column, (9) 'concept debt' list a la tech debt, (10) split industry-concepts vs internally-coined registry. C=gates/lints: (11) jargon-density lint on human surfaces [roadmap], (12) new-concept understanding-gate before a concept becomes load-bearing, (13) unlock-on-teach (term unusable bare until 'taught' logged). D=interactive teaching: (14) tutor agent [user C3, Pocock], (15) inline micro-teaching box folded into flow, (16) explain-back/active-recall checkpoint that OBSERVES familiarity, (17) on-demand 'unpack that' interrupt, (18) spaced re-surfacing of 🟡 until 🟢. E=structural: (19) extend Interrogator remit to run concept-checks at every checkpoint not just intake, (20) teaching as a first-class deliverable / acceptance criterion per epic. Key fork surfaced (NOT decided): who owns the familiarity estimate — agent-guessed (drifts, patronizing) vs user-set (honest, a chore) vs observed-from-explain-back (honest + low-chore, needs the teaching loop). Also a build-vs-extend tension: new machinery (book+tutor) vs extend-what-exists (glossary column + interrogator + inline teaching).

x1.title: X1 research: tutor + familiarity-tracking prior art (Pocock + ecosystem)
x1.imperative: Research excursion, agent-initiated, background via run_crew external backend. Result verified fresh at excursions/x1-tutor-prior-art.md.
x1.finding: Pocock's /teach is deliberately low-tech: intake questionnaire (self-reported level) + a persistent human-co-authored markdown 'learning record'; companion /grill-me quizzes. Scoped null: NO public source, NO numeric mastery score, NO per-concept familiarity vector, NO spaced scheduling. Prior art (BKT, SM-2/Leitner, mastery learning, self-explanation): borrow the shape (per-concept familiarity scalar; time-since-contact decay; dependency-ordered depth) but NOT the math/gating - all classroom mechanisms need a stream of graded responses our architect never emits. Strongest fit = self-explanation: read familiarity off the human's OWN writing (only observation source that exists here). Steer: (1) familiarity-owner fork -> lean observed-from-writing + human-legible shared record, away from agent-guessed numeric vector AND away from user-chore self-rating; (2) build-vs-extend -> lean extend (a markdown record, not a scoring engine). NOT tested: /teach internals, deep-learning KT, FSRS.

consolidation.summary: Cycle 1 (shotgun) consolidated. Point sharpened: the target is (a) real-world/industry concepts the user hasn't met yet (e.g. Materin/Matern process) which they WANT to learn, and (b) low tolerance for internal/project-coined jargon (worse across many concurrent projects); NOT a jargon ban — peer register with precise jargon is wanted, condescension refused. Grade target B->C. No hard kill; soft anti-goals (no heavy machinery for its own sake, no jargon ban, no condescension).
